images.caption: Steam winding engine Davy Bros of sheffield, 1876 horizontal duplex winding engine. Can be turned electrically. I saw this run in the late 1970s when it was used on wednesday mornings to inspect the shaft. The shaft was not in regular use but was maintained as a means of egress. The shaft headgear is unusual (now) in being of wood. The shaft is now in use for underground tours as part of the National Mining Museum.

images.caption: Caphouse Colliery/National Mining Museum One of my favourite views that includes the wooden headgear, 1876 steam winding engine house and the square chimney for the two Lancashire boilers.

images.caption: National Mining Museum The former Caphouse Colliery is the third NMM. The first was at Lound Hall near the NCB's Bevercotes Colliery and the second was at Chatterley Whitfield Colliery. Caphouse has a genuine underground experience. The only other pit in the UK to offer a genuine underground visit is Big Pit, Blaenavon.

images.filename: Coal conveyor drift and fan connection - geograph.org.uk - 1023026.jpg
images.caption: Coal conveyor drift and fan connection At the National Mining Museum, Caphouse Pit, this is a drift into the hillside, where coal was brought out by conveyor, and transferred to a second conveyor that raised it to the pit head area. This drift was (is) also used as the connection point for the ventilation fans.
